[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
No goal experiences were retrieved. Consolidated process lessons: Most action failures are caused by unmet preconditions. Before moving, verify the intended path is clear of obstacles (e.g., a stool) and replan by navigating around, removing, or avoiding the obstruction instead of assuming forward movement will succeed. Before picking up, confirm the target object exists, is visible/reachable, and is near or within reach; if not, navigate to its location first. Before placing, confirm the robot is already holding the target object via a successful pickup. Treat predicted success as conditional, and when an action fails, inspect the violated precondition and replan rather than repeating the same command.

## Preliminary Thinking
1. Parse the task and identify the target object, destination, and required action sequence. 2. Inspect the environment to locate the object, destination, and any obstacles. 3. Before navigation, check that the path is clear; if blocked, navigate around the obstacle, remove it, or choose an alternative route. 4. If the target object is not near, navigate to its location and verify it is visible and reachable. 5. Attempt pickup only after confirming object presence and proximity; then verify the robot is holding it. 6. Navigate toward the destination while checking for and avoiding obstacles. 7. Attempt placement only after verifying the robot is holding the object. 8. Monitor each action result; on failure, diagnose which precondition was violated and replan accordingly.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
